title: Operator goal-text cannot steer or exclude task selection — it is LLM-facing prose, not a selector
summary: Observed live wave 4 (cycles 1575-1577, 2026-08-27): launched with --goal-text naming four preferred inbox items in priority order AND explicitly excluding one console-reserved item. The loop picked NONE of the four preferred items and DID pick the excluded one (transient-artifact-timeout-shortcircuit-the-silence-budget), alongside retro-prompt-delivery-stall and tokenopt-handoff-digests. Traced structurally: GoalText reaches only phase_advisor.go (advisor prompt, truncated to 4000 chars), phase_judge.go, and router.RoutingInput — all LLM-facing context. Lane assignment runs carryoverTodos -> fleet.Partition(todos, n), which takes only the todo list and a lane count and is entirely goal-blind; the sole `exclude` map in internal/fleet (freshness.go RefillFn) is refill dedup so the same id is not launched twice, NOT operator exclusion. CONSEQUENCE: an operator cannot express 'work these, not that' — a directive can only be honored if an LLM reads and obeys prose, and here it did not. This is the same class as the cycle-1571 H2 goal-text insurance clause that an agent executed as 'delete the red test': goal text READS like a control surface and is not one. Also observed: auto-prune reported 764 carryoverTodos with cycles_unpicked incremented on all of them — a very large backlog aging without ever being worked, so whatever the operator files competes with 764 older entries. Fix options: (a) a deterministic pre-partition filter honoring an explicit include/exclude id list passed alongside the goal; (b) a first-class --only/--exclude flag distinct from prose goal text; (c) at minimum, FAIL LOUDLY at launch when goal text names ids that the resolved lane set does not contain, so the operator learns immediately that the directive was inert rather than discovering it three cycles later. LIVE FOLLOW-UP (cycle-1575, same wave, now observed end-to-end): the earlier phrasing 'the loop DID pick the excluded one' is imprecise in a way that would misdirect the fix. The PARTITIONER assigned the excluded id; the AGENTS refused it. Verified: the goal text including the word EXCLUDE is present in all six scout and triage prompts across the three lanes (delivery works). Scout flagged the id as goal-excluded, and triage-report.md emits verdict FAIL with top_n=[] and rationale 'the stated goal explicitly excludes that item as reserved for console ownership. No other item is in this lane's assigned fleet scope, so no candidate is eligible for top_n.' So prose WAS obeyed — by every LLM that read it. The inertness is entirely upstream (fleet.Partition assigns todo_ids before any agent sees the goal) and downstream (the spine dispatched tdd and build anyway; see spine-dispatches-build-after-empty-triage). This raises option (c) — fail loudly at launch when goal text names ids absent from the resolved lane set — from 'at minimum' to the cheapest real fix, since the only thing prose could not do here was reach the partitioner.
